plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and large, rose-like flowers. It thrives in mild, humid climates and is a popular ornamental in gardens and parks, with thousands of cultivars in many forms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early spring (peak in winter)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is closely related to Camellia sinensis, the plant used to make tea, and its seeds are pressed to produce camellia oil used in cooking and cosmetics.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A spreading tree with fern-like leaves and a broad umbrella-shaped canopy that becomes covered in clusters of vivid blossoms. It blooms in the Southern Hemisphere summer, when it is a spectacular sight in warm regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer (December to February); spring to summer in the tropics of the north
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions including Australia, South Africa, and Brazil
plants.funFact: Despite its abundance around the world, the royal poinciana is endangered in its native Madagascar because of habitat loss.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low-growing evergreen perennial with leathery, dark green leaves and nodding, cup-shaped white flowers that age to pink. It flowers in the cold of winter, often pushing through snow in woodlands and gardens.
plants.location: Native to the mountains of central and southern Europe; grown in temperate gardens in Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Although it is called a rose, it is actually a member of the buttercup family and all parts of the plant are poisonous.

plants.name: Hippeastrum hybrids
plants.description: A bulbous perennial producing tall, sturdy stalks topped with several giant trumpet-shaped flowers. Outdoors it blooms in the Southern Hemisphere summer, and in the north it is widely forced indoors for winter display.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer; indoors in Northern Hemisphere winter
plants.location: Native to South America (Andes and Brazil); cultivated worldwide as a houseplant and garden bulb
plants.funFact: A single amaryllis bulb can send up flower stalks that grow several centimeters in a single day, and it can rebloom for many years with proper care.
